questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is an opinion rather than a verifiable fact?
options: The headline national figure tells a smallholder very little about when to sow.
The India Meteorological Department issues a seasonal outlook in April.
Text-message alerts in local languages now reach millions of farmers.
Rainfall in a week can differ between two villages ten kilometres apart.
questions.explanation: The first statement is a judgement made by critics. The others can be checked against records or measurements.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a verifiable fact rather than an opinion?
options: Accepting a UPI payment does not require a card machine.
UPI is the most important financial reform of the decade.
Technology is a smaller challenge than reaching excluded people.
Fear of fraud among the elderly is unjustified.
questions.explanation: Only the first statement can be checked as true or false. The others are judgements.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a verifiable fact according to the passage?
options: Matches have been shortened and some rules adjusted.
The changes have damaged the spirit of the game.
Old village referees would have disliked the music.
Kabaddi has a brighter future than any other rural sport.
questions.explanation: Only the first can be checked. The second is a purist's view, the third is speculation and the fourth is not in the passage.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a judgement rather than a verifiable fact?
options: Moving away from millets was a costly mistake.
Millets can grow on land where rice would fail.
Several state agricultural departments buy millets for school meals.
Ragi, jowar and bajra are millets.
questions.explanation: 'Costly mistake' is an evaluation. The other statements can be checked by agricultural data or records.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an opinion rather than a fact?
options: The best outcome would be a blend of online and board play.
State governments reward medal winners with jobs and prize money.
Viswanathan Anand won a world title.
Online platforms let a child play many games every week.
questions.explanation: 'Best outcome' is a judgement. The other three are reported facts that can be verified.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a speculation rather than a verifiable fact?
options: The cloth may survive better than the craft that produces it.
Power looms can copy an ikat design in a few hours.
The government reserves certain designs for handloom producers.
Ikat threads are tied and dyed before weaving begins.
questions.explanation: The first statement predicts the future ('may survive'). The others describe present, checkable matters.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an opinion or prediction rather than a reported fact?
options: A good idea like telemedicine will succeed if given modest investment.
Doctors report that telemedicine works well for follow-up visits.
A doctor in Chandigarh can consult a villager by video call.
Many state governments have built telemedicine into their health plans.
questions.explanation: The first is a prediction about success. The rest are reported or observable facts.

questions.questionText: In the passage on coaching institutes, which of the following is a verifiable fact rather than an opinion?
options: Some institutes now hold weekly fun events for students.
Coaching fees are a safe investment.
The wellbeing measures merely treat symptoms.
A single rank decides a whole life.
questions.explanation: Only the first can be verified by checking institutes. The others are views or exaggerations.
